segments.text: American Fork City Council — Special and Work Session — June 4, 2024:

entities.speaker: Anna Montoya
entities.remark-context: Police staffing in the proposed budget

segments.text: Finance Officer Anna Montoya told the council that the proposed fiscal-year 2025 budget included two additional police officers.

entities.label: Two additional police officers in the proposed budget

segments.text: The fiscal-year 2025 budget proposal included two new police-officer positions.
Relevant passage from the official meeting minutes:

Ms. Montoya stated that there was a change this year. Road Capital projects fund was separated from the General Capital projects just so we can track that a little bit better. She mentioned it will move over to the fund balance after the audits to make sure that there are dedicated funds specifically for roads. She commented that she will bring forth the Certified Rate by next week when the budget gets approved and there will be no tax increase for this budget but is still waiting on the county to give those numbers to get the approval for next week.

She mentioned that Station 53 site analysis and concept design is included in the budget for $50,000. Ms. Montoya added that there was $250,000 included for the downtown revitalization plan to get the ball rolling in the downtown area. She commented that are some FTE changes (see page 67 of Budget Book for explanation of charges).

• The communications position went from part-time to full-time.
• Parks has an additional 1.5 part-time season laborers.
• Senior Center proposing a full-time administrative assistant or Senior Manager from part-time.
• Police department – adding 2 additional police officers.
• Fire department – adding 1.25 part-time firefighters to help with overtime costs.
• Engineering added one full GIS technician.
• Fitness Center allocation from the Senior Center Manager – it will be split between both.

entities.label: Victim Assistance Program responsibilities and service volume

segments.text: AFPD victim advocates described their role following violent crime, including safety planning, referrals, protective orders, stalking injunctions, court notifications, and communication among victims, officers, investigators, prosecutors, and community providers.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Report by Dawna Whiting on the American Fork Victim’s Assistance program.

Ms. Whiting and Ms. Nordin introduced themselves and introduced Carrie Getty who has volunteered for many years with this program. AFPD VA provides:

• Post-crisis supports to Victims of all violent crime.
• Assess needs and provide referrals, assist with obtaining services.
• Victims with appropriate educational and preventative information, develop safety plans and goals.
• Act as liaison between victim, police officers, investigators, prosecutors, and community-based agencies.
• Assist with applications for Crime Victims Reparations which provides reparation for therapy and reimbursement for abuse related medical bills.
• Asses need for and assist with obtaining Protective Orders or Stalking injunctions.
• Monitor Perpetrator court appearance and provide Victim with updates and court notifications, inform victims of their rights and protect their interest.
• Aim to decrease recidivism, ensure victim safety, and hold batterer accountable.

Ms. Whiting went over the number of victims they have served from October 2023 to March 2024.

• 637 victims contacted.
• 2,911 total services/assist.

Ms. Whiting commented about the differences in numbers that they get from the number of victims versus the number of calls that they make, and it’s based on the victims’ needs. She reported they do all their normal intake with victims and call them to get a feel of what they need and how they can give them help through the next couple of months. She added they never know what the victims may need and go from there.

Ms. Whiting reported that some of the victims aren’t all Police department victims, they could also be children of victims.

Discussion about victim percentages and type of victims ensued between the AFPD VA board members and the Council.

Ms. Whiting commented that anytime she counts a new victim in the quarter for the grant, it’s a new case, new victim and the services should be duplicated throughout other quarters. She added that her services could be duplicated throughout other quarters. Ms. Nordin mentioned that when they call the victims and give them resources, they track each time they give some type of help during that phone call or in person visit with them.

Ms. Whiting did state the trend she is seeing is everyone is angrier and more demanding. She added most of the victims’ age range from 25 to 48 years old. The mayor thanked the board for their report. Mr. Bunker mentioned that Chief Paul has great things to say about the Victim’s Advocate program and how needed they are.
